Content:
A pyramid's altitude (or height) is the line segment perpendicular to the base and connects the base to the apex (shown above).

Content:
The volume [MATH: V] of the pyramid is given by

Content:
[MATH: V = \dfrac{1}{3}Ah]

Content:
where [MATH: A] is the area of the base, and [MATH: h] is the height.

Content:
For example, suppose the base area of a pyramid is [MATH: 12 \, \textrm{in}^2] and its altitude is [MATH: 4 \, \textrm{in}.] Substituting

Content:
[MATH: A=12\,\textrm{in}^2, \qquad
h=4\,\textrm{in}]

Content:
into the formula for [MATH: V,] we get

Content:
[MATH: V = \dfrac{1}{3} (12) (4) = 16 \: \text{in}^3.]

sections.normalized_html: Determine the volume of the pyramid shown below.

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
We can find the volume of a pyramid using the formula

[MATH: V = \dfrac{1}{3}Ah,]

where [MATH: A] is the area of the base and [MATH: h] is the altitude of the pyramid.

Substituting [MATH: A=15\,\textrm{cm}^2] and [MATH: h=7\,\textrm{cm}] into the formula, we get

[MATH: V = \dfrac{1}{3} (15) (7) = 35 \: \text{cm}^3.]

sections.readable_text:
Consider the pyramid [MATH: SBCD] below, where [MATH: \triangle{BCD}] is the base and [MATH: \overline{SH}] is the altitude. Find the volume of the pyramid given that [MATH: BD=9\,\textrm{in},] [MATH: CL=7\,\textrm{in},] and [MATH: SH=8\,\textrm{in}.]

[IMG: /graphics/bb5557de1a51ae09eaa01dee32a5914a]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
We can find the volume of a pyramid using the formula

[MATH: V = \dfrac{1}{3}Ah,]

where [MATH: A] is the area of the base and [MATH: h] is the altitude of the pyramid.

Now, notice the following:

  • We are told that [MATH: \overline{SH}] is the altitude of the pyramid. So, we have [MATH: h=SH=8\,\textrm{in}.]

  • The line segment [MATH: \overline{CL}] is the height of [MATH: \triangle{BCD}] corresponding to the side [MATH: \overline{BD}.] So, we compute the area of [MATH: \triangle{BCD}] as [MATH: A|= (BD ⋅ CL)/(2); = (9 ⋅ 7)/(2); = (63)/(2)in^{2}.]

Finally, substituting [MATH: A= \dfrac{63}{2}\,\textrm{in}^2] and [MATH: h=8\,\textrm{in}] into the formula, we get

[MATH: V = \dfrac{1}{3} \left( \dfrac{63}{2}\right) (8) = 84 \: \text{in}^3.]

[IMG: /graphics/82e7b1db6c20a0cc3194a63a30d9324a]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Recall that we can find the volume of a pyramid using the formula

[MATH: V = \dfrac{1}{3}Ah,]

where [MATH: A] is the area of the base and [MATH: h] is the altitude of the pyramid.

Notice that [MATH: \overline{BH}] is the height of [MATH: \triangle{BCD}] corresponding to the side [MATH: \overline{CD}.] So, we compute the area of [MATH: \triangle{BCD}] as

[MATH: A|= (BH ⋅ CD)/(2); = (10 ⋅ 21)/(2); = 105cm^{2}.]

Next, we substitute

[MATH: V = 385 \, \textrm{cm}^3, \qquad A = 105 \, \textrm{cm}^2]

into the formula for [MATH: V] and solve for [MATH: h,] as follows:

[MATH: V|= (1)/(3)Ah; 385|= (1)/(3)(105)h; 385|= 35h; h|= 11]

Therefore, [MATH: SH=h=11 \, \textrm{cm}.]

items.title: Finding the Volume of a Pyramid Using the Pythagorean Theorem

sections.normalized_html: Consider the pyramid above, where the base is a square, and the height passes through the center of the base. Find the volume of the pyramid.
sections.readable_text:
[IMG: /graphics/e460d59f3cde6637d9511342386c70ce]

Consider the pyramid above, where the base is a square, and the height passes through the center of the base. Find the volume of the pyramid.

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
We can find the volume of a pyramid using the formula

[MATH: V = \dfrac{1}{3}Ah,]

where [MATH: A] is the area of the base and [MATH: h] is the altitude of the pyramid.

Notice that [MATH: \triangle{SHL}] is a right triangle, and

[MATH: HL = \dfrac{24}{2} = 12 \, \textrm{in}.]

Using the Pythagorean theorem, we obtain the following:

[MATH: SH^{2} + HL^{2}|= SL^{2}; SH^{2} + (12)^{2}|= (15)^{2}; SH^{2} + 144|= 225; SH^{2}|= 81; SH|= 9in]

The area of the base is given by

[MATH: A = 24^2 = 576 \, \textrm{in}^2.]

Therefore, the volume is

[MATH: V = \dfrac{1}{3}(576)(9)= 1\,728 \, \textrm{in}^3.]

Notice that [MATH: \triangle{SHL}] is a right triangle, and

[MATH: HL = \dfrac{24}{2} = 12 \, \textrm{in}.]

Using the Pythagorean theorem, we obtain the following:

[MATH: SH^{2} + HL^{2}|= SL^{2}; SH^{2} + (12)^{2}|= (15)^{2}; SH^{2} + 144|= 225; SH^{2}|= 81; SH|= 9in]
